outputs.L1:
We define nonselfadjoint operator algebras generated by \(L_{e_1}, \ldots, L_{e_n}, L_{f_1}, \ldots, L_{f_m}\), subject to unitary commutation relations of the form
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
=
\sum_{k,l} u_{i,j,k,l}\,L_{f_l}L_{e_k},
\]
where \(u=(u_{i,j,k,l})\) is an \(nm \times nm\) unitary matrix. These algebras generalise the analytic Toeplitz algebras associated with single-vertex rank-2 graphs and are classified, up to isometric isomorphism, in terms of the matrix \(u\).
outputs.L2:
We study nonselfadjoint operator algebras generated by \(L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n}\) and \(L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}\), with multiplication governed by the unitary relations
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
=
\sum_{k,l} u_{i,j,k,l}\,L_{f_l}L_{e_k},
\]
where \(u=(u_{i,j,k,l})\) is an \(nm\times nm\) unitary matrix. This family extends the analytic Toeplitz algebras associated with single-vertex rank-2 graphs. Moreover, its members are classified, up to isometric isomorphism, by the defining matrix \(u\).
outputs.L3:
Nonselfadjoint operator algebras of this type are generated by two families of creation operators,
\[
L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}.
\]
These operators act on an appropriate Fock space and represent two distinct kinds, or “colors,” of edges. Unlike generators of a selfadjoint operator algebra, their adjoints are not generally included in the algebra.

The interaction between the two families is encoded by an \(nm\times nm\) unitary matrix \(u\). In a standard convention, the generators satisfy relations of the form
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
   =\sum_{k=1}^{n}\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}
     u_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}\,L_{f_\ell}L_{e_k}.
\]
Thus, \(u\) specifies how a product involving an \(e\)-generator followed by an \(f\)-generator can be rewritten with the order reversed. The unitarity of \(u\) ensures that these commutation rules are compatible with the underlying Hilbert-space structure.

These algebras generalize the analytic Toeplitz algebras associated with single-vertex rank-2 graphs. In the graph setting, commutation is typically governed by a permutation matrix, corresponding to a factorization rule for paths of different colors. Allowing \(u\) to be an arbitrary unitary matrix replaces this discrete permutation rule with a more general unitary change of basis.

The matrix \(u\) therefore serves as the central invariant of the construction. Up to the natural changes of basis in the two families of generators—and, where appropriate, interchange of the two families—the isometric isomorphism class of the resulting nonselfadjoint operator algebra is determined by the equivalence class of \(u\). Consequently, classifying these algebras reduces to understanding the relevant unitary equivalence relations among their defining matrices.
outputs.L4:
Let \(n,m\geq 1\), and let \(u\) be a unitary matrix on \(\mathbb C^{n}\otimes\mathbb C^{m}\). Associated with \(u\) is a Fock-type Hilbert space carrying two families of left creation operators,
\[
L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n}
    \quad\text{and}\quad
L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}.
\]
The interaction between the two families is prescribed by \(u\): products of an \(e\)-generator with an \(f\)-generator can be rewritten as linear combinations of products in the opposite order, with coefficients given by the entries of \(u\). Thus one obtains unitary commutation relations of the form
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
   =\sum_{k=1}^{n}\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}
      u_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}\,L_{f_\ell}L_{e_k},
\]
up to the chosen indexing convention.

The norm-closed, generally nonselfadjoint operator algebra generated by these creation operators and the identity is denoted by \(\mathcal A_u\). It may be regarded as the tensor algebra of the product system determined by \(u\). When \(u\) is a permutation matrix, the relations are combinatorial: each word \(e_i f_j\) is identified with a single word \(f_\ell e_k\). In that case, \(\mathcal A_u\) recovers the analytic Toeplitz algebra associated with a single-vertex rank-2 graph. Allowing an arbitrary unitary matrix replaces these permutation relations by linear unitary relations and therefore gives a broader class of operator algebras.

A central issue is whether the defining commutation data can be recovered from the algebra itself. The classification theorem shows that it can. More precisely, two such algebras \(\mathcal A_u\) and \(\mathcal A_v\) are isometrically isomorphic exactly when their defining unitary matrices are equivalent under the natural changes of orthonormal bases in the two families of generators, together with any admissible interchange of the two coordinate directions. Consequently, the isometric isomorphism class of \(\mathcal A_u\) is completely determined by the corresponding equivalence class of \(u\).

The proof analyzes the character space and the behavior of an isometric isomorphism on the degree-one generators. These invariants force an isomorphism to respect the two generator families, except in the symmetric situation where the families may be exchanged. The commutation relations then imply that the induced unitary changes of variables must carry the matrix \(u\) to the matrix defining the target algebra. Conversely, every such equivalence of unitary data produces an isometric isomorphism of the associated operator algebras.

This result extends the classification of analytic Toeplitz algebras arising from single-vertex rank-2 graphs. It shows that, even for general unitary rather than purely combinatorial commutation relations, the nonselfadjoint operator algebra retains the full structure of its defining unitary matrix.
outputs.L5: These matrices, known as **Toeplitz matrices**, have constant values along each diagonal from left to right. Their regular structure makes them useful in signal processing, time-series analysis, image restoration, and numerical computation. Because a Toeplitz matrix can be described using only its first row and first column, it requires less storage than a general matrix and often enables faster algorithms. These properties make Toeplitz matrices especially valuable when modeling systems whose behavior is invariant over time or space.

counterfactuals.prompt: Define the nonselfadjoint operator algebras generated by \(L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n}\) and \(L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}\) with unitary commutation relations, and briefly state their classification.
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(E=\mathbb C^{n}\), \(F=\mathbb C^{m}\), and let  
\[
u:E\otimes F\longrightarrow F\otimes E
\]
be unitary. With fixed bases \(\{e_i\}\) and \(\{f_j\}\), impose the relations
\[
e_i f_j=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}
u_{(i,j),(\ell,k)}\,f_\ell e_k .
\]

On the product-system Fock space
\[
\mathcal F_u=\bigoplus_{p,q\ge 0} E^{\otimes p}\otimes F^{\otimes q},
\]
let \(L_{e_i}\) and \(L_{f_j}\) be the corresponding left creation operators. They satisfy the same unitary commutation relations. Define

\[
\mathcal A_u=
\overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|}
\{I,L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n},L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}\},
\]
the **unitary relation tensor algebra**, and
\[
\mathcal L_u=
\overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\,\mathrm{WOT}}
\{I,L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n},L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}\},
\]
the associated **unitary relation free semigroup/Hardy algebra**.

Their completely isometric classification is determined by the dimensions \((n,m)\) and the product-unitary equivalence class of \(u\): \(u\) and \(v\) give isomorphic graded algebras precisely when there are unitaries \(A:E\to E'\) and \(B:F\to F'\) such that
\[
v=(B\otimes A)\,u\,(A\otimes B)^*.
\]
If interchange of the two generator families is allowed, one also identifies \(u\) with the corresponding flipped inverse relation \(u^{-1}\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract-style description of unitary relation algebras that generalize analytic Toeplitz algebras of single-vertex rank-2 graphs.
counterfactuals.output:
Given a unitary \(U\in M_{mn}(\mathbb C)\), the unitary relation algebra \(\mathcal A_U\) is the nonselfadjoint operator algebra generated by row isometries \(e_1,\ldots,e_m\) and \(f_1,\ldots,f_n\) satisfying
\[
e_i f_j=\sum_{k,\ell} U_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}\, f_\ell e_k .
\]
It is realized as the norm-closed algebra generated by the corresponding creation operators on a product-system Fock space over \(\mathbb N^2\). When \(U\) is a permutation unitary, these relations recover the factorization rules of a single-vertex rank-2 graph, and \(\mathcal A_U\) is its analytic Toeplitz algebra. Allowing arbitrary unitaries replaces combinatorial commutation by unitary mixing, yielding a broader class whose representation theory, character spaces, automorphisms, and isomorphism invariants reflect the geometry of \(U\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: How are operator algebras satisfying \(L_{e_i}L_{f_j}=\sum_{k,l}u_{i,j,k,l}L_{f_l}L_{e_k}\) defined and classified up to isometric isomorphism?
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(E=\mathbb C^{m}\) and \(F=\mathbb C^{n}\), with orthonormal bases \(\{e_i\}\) and \(\{f_j\}\). Choose a unitary
\[
u:E\otimes F\longrightarrow F\otimes E,
\qquad
u(e_i\otimes f_j)
 =\sum_{k,l}u_{i,j,k,l}\,f_l\otimes e_k .
\]

This unitary defines a product system over \(\mathbb N^2\): whenever an \(E\)-letter passes an \(F\)-letter, it is rewritten using \(u\). Its Fock space can be written
\[
\mathcal F_u=\bigoplus_{p,q\ge 0} E^{\otimes p}\otimes F^{\otimes q},
\]
with the identifications between different word orders implemented by tensor powers of \(u\).

The left creation operators are
\[
L_{e_i}\xi=e_i\otimes \xi,\qquad
L_{f_j}\xi=f_j\otimes \xi,
\]
where \(u\) is used to place tensors into the chosen normal order. They satisfy
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
   =\sum_{k,l}u_{i,j,k,l}L_{f_l}L_{e_k}.
\]
The associated unitary-relation or tensor algebra is
\[
\mathcal A_u
   =\overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|}
      \{I,L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_m},L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_n}\}.
\]
Equivalently, it is the universal norm-closed operator algebra generated by two row contractions satisfying the above unitary commutation relations.

### Isometric-isomorphism classification

Two unitaries
\[
u:E\otimes F\to F\otimes E,
\qquad
v:E'\otimes F'\to F'\otimes E'
\]
are **product-unitarily equivalent** if there are unitaries
\[
A:E\to E',\qquad B:F\to F'
\]
such that
\[
v(A\otimes B)=(B\otimes A)u.
\]
This precisely corresponds to independent unitary changes of the \(e\)- and \(f\)-generators.

The classification theorem is:

- A color-preserving isometric isomorphism
  \(\mathcal A_u\simeq\mathcal A_v\) exists exactly when
  \[
  \dim E=\dim E',\qquad \dim F=\dim F',
  \]
  and \(u,v\) are product-unitarily equivalent.

- The two colors may also be interchanged. In that case the dimensions are swapped and \(v\) must be product-unitarily equivalent to the opposite relation
  \[
  u^{\mathrm{op}}=u^{-1}:F\otimes E\longrightarrow E\otimes F.
  \]

Thus, up to isometric—and in fact completely isometric—isomorphism,
\[
\boxed{\mathcal A_u\cong\mathcal A_v}
\]
if and only if the unordered dimension pairs agree and either \(u\) and \(v\) are product-unitarily equivalent, or one becomes product-unitarily equivalent to the inverse relation after exchanging the two generator families. For fixed \(m=n\), this is often stated as classification by product-unitary equivalence “up to flip.”
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main result of a paper on nonselfadjoint operator algebras determined by an \(nm\times nm\) unitary matrix \(u\).
counterfactuals.output:
The paper associates to each \(nm\times nm\) unitary \(u\) a universal nonselfadjoint operator algebra \(\mathcal A_u\), generated by two row contractions satisfying the unitary commutation relations encoded by \(u\). Its main result is a classification theorem:

\[
\mathcal A_u \cong_{\mathrm{c.i.}} \mathcal A_v
\]

if and only if \(u\) and \(v\) are equivalent under independent unitary changes of basis in the \(n\)- and \(m\)-generator families—called **product-unitary equivalence**—with the additional possibility of interchanging the two families when their sizes permit it. Thus, up to the natural flip symmetry, the operator algebra completely remembers the product-unitary equivalence class of the defining matrix.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain in one short paragraph how analytic Toeplitz algebras of rank-2 graphs with one vertex can be generalized using unitary commutation relations among their generators.
counterfactuals.output:
For a one-vertex rank-2 graph, the analytic Toeplitz algebra is generated by two row-isometric families \(S_1,\dots,S_m\) and \(T_1,\dots,T_n\), with mixed products determined by a permutation relation. This is generalized by replacing the permutation matrix with any unitary \(U\in M_{mn}(\mathbb C)\) and imposing
\[
S_iT_j=\sum_{k,\ell}U_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}\,T_\ell S_k.
\]
The resulting norm-closed algebra, represented by creation operators on the associated product-system Fock space, is a unitary-commutation or \(U\)-twisted analytic Toeplitz algebra; ordinary rank-2 graph algebras occur when \(U\) is a permutation matrix.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
